comments: 100-150 present. Observed 100-200 meters off the coast. Possibility of Stejneger's Scoter in the flock.
Observed dive bombing. Very far away from the coast.
Observed foraging on ground around 19:00. Martins and Bank swallow was there in the flock.

two adults flew north amongst common tern flock. Same size as common terns but distinctly paler, narrow dark bill (bit distant to see if red had developed at base or not). One bird had longer streamers, both with dark wedge on leading edge of primaries on upperwing.
Not 100% sure if it was one but they are spotted here and it was a grey pigeon sizes bird flapping like a falcon with bright red feet but it was flying and hard to see.
All together flying over Arthur’s Seat. Vocalizing

comments: 2 flying west and another 2 chasing gulls very distantly.

Fairly distant but I could still notice some distinct features: Was straight winged, all dark, arced in flight before gliding over the water (lost it very shortly after) and was noticeably bigger than a Manx Shearwater. Although this sighting was brief and even recent human memory can be inaccurate at times, unless it was a rarity (Like a Cory's or any other rare Shearwater) I'm fairly certain it was a Sooty.
Female, has been moulting here for some time.

comments: Curlew next to an oystercatcher of which it was the same size.
Flew by very close to the seawall. Sterna type tern with obvious long tail streamers. Had to sacrifice getting a photo to protect my camera from the horrible weather.
Two putative males together with Common Eiders. Surf Scoters werr separated from the big Velvet group!
The same group that seen by many birders  at the see wall!

Two males managed to glimpse with the tremendous flock of Velvets as they were getting closer to the shore after 19.00 pm. Distinctive bill shape from profile and the conspicous elongated white eyebrow mark help to separate them from Velvets at close range.
